Both test classes compile successfully.

## Summary

Created two self-contained JUnit 5 test classes based strictly on the documented contracts in `api/`:

**`tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/AnnotationUtilsAgentTest.java`**
- Uses a nested custom `@Sample` annotation (and a second `@Other` type) applied to fields, retrieved via reflection, to get real `Annotation` instances to exercise `equals`, `hashCode`, and `toString`.
- Covers `equals`: both-null, one-null (each side), reflexive, equal/unequal member values, differing annotation types.
- Covers `hashCode`: equal-annotations-equal-hash, differing values produce different hash, stability; and — using hand-built `Proxy`/`InvocationHandler` annotation instances — the documented `IllegalStateException` (member returns `null`) and `RuntimeException` (exception during member access) cases.
- Covers `isValidAnnotationMemberType`: `String`, `Class`, all primitives, annotation types, enums, single-dimensional arrays (valid) vs. multi-dimensional arrays and arbitrary classes (invalid).
- Covers `toString`: non-null, `@TypeName(member=value, ...)` shape, differs for different values.
- Covers the deprecated public constructor.

**`tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/AbstractReflectionAgentTest.java`**
- Defines minimal concrete `AbstractBuilder`/`AbstractReflection` subclasses (required since both are abstract with package-private constructors — accessible because the test lives in the same package).
- Covers `getForceAccessible()` against the `AbstractReflection.forceAccessible` system property (unset/true/false/case-insensitivity/non-boolean), saving and restoring the property around each test.
- Covers builder `setForceAccessible` (fluent return) and `isForceAccessible()` propagation from the builder to the built instance.
- Covers the static `setAccessible(boolean, AccessibleObject)` and package-private instance `setAccessible(Field)`, using genuinely private fields to deterministically verify accessible/inaccessible transitions and the null-handling/already-accessible edge cases from the docs.
- Gives lighter, name-justified smoke coverage to the undocumented package-private `register`/`isRegistered`/`unregister`/`toRegisterPair` helpers (no prose contract exists for these in the javadoc), asserting only what their signatures/names clearly imply (registry mutation, round-trip membership).

`./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`.
